title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'Flashing Lights', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the tambourine: wooden rim, a pale skin head, eight paired brass jingles; whole in this poem (held out by the ghost, in two small hands, cocked back, flying through the glass, still whole); the living-room window: a big front window with casing, mullions and sill, venetian blinds and a floral curtain; the one glass in the film that breaks (blinds down, blinds up, struck, shattered, the room peeling to black); the height marks: seven pencil notches on a white door post, cut by hand, slightly kinked (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (appearing one by one, complete: six and seven); the mirror: full-length standing mirror, dark frame, a clock seen only in its glass (dark, his hand flat on it, met by its own); the engagement rings: two plain gold rings (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (approaching, never touching, on the sill, sliding apart); the phone: smartphone face-up on the sheets, screen glowing (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (dark, ringing twice); the family car: 1990s sedan, headlights and amber hazards (cresting the bumps, idling, dome light on, rolling down the road, hazards flashing); blinds and cord: white venetian slats and a pull cord (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (down, lifting from the bottom, all the way up); the Tide Office notice: a small white enamel plate on the lamppost by the curb: two lines, the next two gates and their heights (dark, headlit). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
